title: Contract induced by lockstep simulation
statement: Let $C$ be a contract for a machine $M$ with entry $e$ and exits $X$, and let a lockstep simulation encode configurations of $M$ into configurations of a machine $N$, with target exit set $X'$ and per-configuration cost. Fix a target entry state $e'$ and integer-valued lower and upper bounds $b_{lo}(c,j)$ and $b_{hi}(c,j)$ for each target work tape $j$. Suppose that the target head position at every encoded configuration after $v$ steps lies within these bounds whenever $v=0$, or whenever the source state is outside $X$ and $v$ is at most its cost. Then there is a contract for $N$, indexed by pairs $(i,c)$, whose precondition requires a configuration equal to $enc(c)$ with $c$ in state $e$ and satisfying $C$’s precondition. Its running time is the sum of the simulation costs over the source run up to (but excluding) $C$’s endpoint; its endpoint is the encoding of $C$’s endpoint; and its work-head bounds are the minimum and maximum of the supplied bounds over the source run, including the endpoint.
